chosen_property.label: object
chosen_property.justification: The 'object' property directly indicates the thing upon which an action or event is carried out, fitting all instances where events target various entities.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property directly links an event to its physical place, matching the observed signatures.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: The 'participant' property directly indicates an entity taking part in an action, fitting all instances where various entities participate in events.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

relations.definition: Indicates the result or consequence of an event or action.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_outcome: Indicates the result or consequence of an event or action.

chosen_property.label: result
chosen_property.justification: The 'result' property directly indicates the outcome generated by an action, matching the observed signature.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: The 'instrument' property indicates a tool used to perform an action, which fits the definition of 'uses_tool' for events.

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: recipe
candidates.comment: A recipe relation between a cook action and the specific recipe used as an instrument. Also called recipe used, instructions for, cooking guide. Examples: "A cook action uses the recipe 'Classic Lasagna'.", "Baking a cake uses the recipe 'Chocolate Fudge Cake'.", "Preparing dinner uses the recipe 'Chicken Stir-fry'."

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

chosen_property.label: usesVehicle
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that an event or action employs a specific vehicle.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links an event to a vehicle used for transport, so a new property is minted as a sub-property of 'instrument'.

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: fuelConsumption
candidates.comment: A fuel consumption relation between a vehicle and the amount of fuel it uses to travel a specific distance or duration. Also called: fuel usage, gas mileage (inverse), liters per 100km. Examples: "Compact Car" fuel consumption "7 L/100 km", "SUV" fuel consumption "12 L/100 km", "Electric Car" fuel consumption "15 kWh/100 km". Distinct from fuelEfficiency, which is a reciprocal measure (distance per unit fuel).

candidates.label: vehicleConfiguration
candidates.comment: A vehicle configuration relation between a vehicle and a short text describing its specific setup. Also called vehicle setup, car configuration, model description. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration '5dr hatchback ST 2.5 MT 225 hp'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'limited edition'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'AWD, leather seats'".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: bodyType
candidates.comment: A qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the design and body style of a vehicle. Also called: vehicle style, car type, chassis type. Examples: "Vehicle 'Ford Focus' bodyType 'Hatchback'", "Vehicle 'Mercedes C-Class' bodyType 'Sedan'."

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: vehicleEngine
candidates.comment: A vehicle engine relation between a vehicle and information about its engine(s). Also called engine details, motor specification, power unit. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'V8 engine'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'Electric motor'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine '2.0L Turbocharged'".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime

candidates.label: scheduledTime

candidates.label: startDate

candidates.label: doorTime

candidates.label: duration

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. candidates.label: endDate

candidates.label: temporalCoverage

Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: byDay

Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

relations.definition: Indicates the specific place where an event or action occurs.
relations.embedding_query_text: at_location: Indicates the specific place where an event or action occurs.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property directly links an event to its physical place, matching the observed signature.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: exerciseCourse
candidates.comment: An exercise course relation between an exercise action and the specific place or course where the action was performed. Also called: workout location, training venue, activity course. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise course "Central Park Loop", "Swimming Practice" exercise course "Olympic Pool Lane 3", "Cycling Race" exercise course "Mountain Bike Trail". Distinct from fromLocation, which is the original location before the action.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: course
candidates.comment: A location relation between an exercise action and the course where it was performed. Also called: exercise location, training course, activity venue. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

relations.definition: Indicates that a subject employs specific equipment to perform an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: uses_equipment: Indicates that a subject employs specific equipment to perform an action.

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: The 'instrument' property indicates a tool or means used to perform an action, which fits the definition of 'uses_equipment' for events.

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: procedure
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the procedure for setting up, using, or installing a medical device. Also called usage instructions, installation guide, operational steps. Examples: A medical device has a procedure for 'surgical implantation'. The equipment includes a procedure for 'daily calibration'. The device's procedure outlines 'user operation steps'.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

chosen_property.label: accesses

candidates.label: requiresSubscription

Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: accessMode
candidates.comment: An access mode relation between a creative work and the human sensory or cognitive system through which its content can be perceived. Also called perceptual mode, sensory access, content modality. Examples: "A video's access mode is 'visual'.", "An audiobook's access mode is 'auditory'.", "A text document's access mode is 'textual'."

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: permissionType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute indicating the specific type of permission granted within a digital document permission. Also called access level, authorization type, privilege type. Examples: A digital document permission has a permission type of 'ReadPermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'WritePermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'CommentPermission'.

candidates.label: accessModeSufficient
candidates.comment: A sufficient access mode relation between a creative work and a list of access modes that are adequate for understanding its full intellectual content. Also called sufficient perceptual modes, adequate access methods. Examples: "A captioned video's sufficient access modes are 'visual' and 'textual'.", "A podcast with a transcript's sufficient access modes are 'auditory' and 'textual'."

candidates.label: accessibilityFeature
candidates.comment: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."

candidates.label: conditionsOfAccess
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, detailing the natural language conditions affecting its availability or access methods. Also called "access restrictions", "availability terms", "usage conditions". Examples: "Archival document conditionsOfAccess 'Available by appointment only'", "Digital artwork conditionsOfAccess 'Requires institutional login'".

candidates.label: accessibilitySummary
candidates.comment: An accessibility summary relation between a creative work and a human-readable text describing its accessibility features and deficiencies. Also called accessibility overview, access statement, accessibility report. Examples: "A website's accessibility summary states 'Short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users'.", "A document's accessibility summary notes 'Fully navigable by keyboard'."

candidates.label: issuedThrough

Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: availableChannel

Examples: "Service 'Customer Support' availableChannel 'Phone Line'", "Service 'Online Banking' availableChannel 'Website'", "Service 'Consultation' availableChannel 'Physical Location'."

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod

Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: providesService

Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService

Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: administrationRoute
candidates.comment: An administration route relation between a drug and the method by which it is intended to be given. Also called dosage route, delivery method, intake method. Examples: "A medication's administration route is 'oral'.", "An injection's administration route is 'intravenous'."

candidates.label: transmissionMethod

Examples: "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'direct contact'", "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'Aedes aegypti'", "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'airborne droplets'".

candidates.label: deliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A logistical approach relation between an order, receive, send, or track action and the method used for delivery. Also called: shipping method, delivery mode, transport method. Examples: "Online Purchase" delivery method "Standard Shipping", "Document Send" delivery method "Email", "Package Tracking" delivery method "Courier Service".

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. candidates.label: itinerary

relations.definition: Indicates that a subject holds or encloses an object within itself.
relations.embedding_query_text: contains: Indicates that a subject holds or encloses an object within itself.

chosen_property.label: contains
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a subject holds or encloses an object within itself.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly captures a general containment relationship between a piece of furniture and a product collection, so a new property is minted as a sub-property of 'hasPart'.

candidates.label: geoContains
candidates.comment: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork
candidates.comment: An encodes creative work relation between a media object and the creative work it represents or contains. Also called "represents work", "contains work", "media of work". Examples: "Video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "Audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Title'", "Image file encodesCreativeWork 'Painting Title'". Distinct from encoding, which is the inverse relation (CreativeWork -> MediaObject).

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

chosen_property.label: source

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". candidates.label: result

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. candidates.label: adverseOutcome

candidates.label: affectedBy

Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemNumber '001'", "OrderItem B orderItemNumber 'SKU-456'", "OrderItem C orderItemNumber 'LITM-789'". Distinct from orderNumber, which identifies the entire order.

candidates.label: orderDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an order was placed. Also called date of order, purchase date, transaction date. Examples: "Order 123 orderDate '2023-10-27'", "Online Purchase orderDate '2023-10-26T10:00:00'", "Subscription Order orderDate '2023-09-01'". Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is when payment is expected.

candidates.label: orderedItem
candidates.comment: An item (product, service, or another order item) that has been ordered. Also called purchased item, item in order, ordered product. Examples: "Order 123 orderedItem 'Laptop X'", "OrderItem A orderedItem 'Software License'", "Subscription Order orderedItem 'Premium Service'".

candidates.label: orderItemStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an order item. Also called item status, line item status, fulfillment status. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "OrderItem B orderItemStatus 'OrderShipped'", "OrderItem C orderItemStatus 'OrderDelivered'". Distinct from orderStatus, which is for the entire order.

candidates.label: orderDelivery
candidates.comment: A parcel delivery associated with an order or order item. Also called delivery details, shipment, parcel tracking. Examples: "Order 123 orderDelivery 'Tracking Number XYZ'", "OrderItem A orderDelivery 'Delivered by UPS'", "Purchase Order orderDelivery 'Scheduled for next week'".

candidates.label: orderValue
candidates.comment: A monetary amount representing the minimum or maximum order value for which specific shipping conditions are valid. Also called order total threshold, shipping value limit, purchase amount condition. Examples: "Free Shipping orderValue '$50.00'", "Discounted Shipping orderValue 'min $100.00'", "Special Rate Shipping orderValue 'max $20.00'". Distinct from orderPercentage, which is a rate based on order value.

chosen_property.label: hasPart
chosen_property.justification: The 'hasPart' property directly models a creative work containing another creative work, fitting a collection including another collection.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: geoContains
candidates.comment: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: position

candidates.label: item
candidates.comment: A list element relation between a data feed item or list item and the entity it represents within a collection. Also called represents, refers to, entry, element. Examples: A list item has an item of 'John Doe'. A data feed item has an item of 'Product X'. A list entry has an item of 'Event Y'.

candidates.label: itemListOrder
candidates.comment: A list arrangement relation between an item list and the specified order of its elements. Also called list sorting, order of items, list sequence, arrangement type. Examples: An item list has itemListOrder 'Ascending'. An item list has itemListOrder 'Descending'. An item list has itemListOrder 'Unordered'.

candidates.label: catalog
candidates.comment: A containment relation between a dataset and the data catalog that holds it. Also called "contained in catalog", "part of catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: "Census data dataset catalog National Data Archive", "Research dataset catalog University Data Repository".

candidates.label: itemListElement
candidates.comment: A list composition relation between an item list and its individual elements, which can be simple text, existing entities, or list items with additional context. Also called list components, list entries, elements of list, items in list. Examples: An item list has itemListElement 'First Item'. An item list has itemListElement 'Product A'. An item list has itemListElement a ListItem for 'Task 1'. Distinct from item, which refers to the entity *within* a ListItem, not the ListItem itself or a direct string/entity in the list.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: collectionSize
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a collection, indicating the total number of items it contains. Also called "number of items", "collection count", "size of collection". Examples: "Art collection collectionSize 500", "Dataset collection collectionSize 10000".

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: catalogNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a music release and its unique catalog number. Also called "release ID", "record label number", "product number". Examples: "Album release catalogNumber 'ABC-123'", "Single release catalogNumber 'XYZ-456'".

Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: yearBuilt

candidates.label: totalHistoricalEnrollment

Also called cumulative enrollment, past enrollment count, historical student count. Examples: "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '500'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '1200'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '75'".

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: birthPlace
candidates.comment: A place where a person was born. Also called: place of birth, birthplace. Examples: "Person 'Albert Einstein' birthPlace 'Ulm, Germany'", "Person 'Marie Curie' birthPlace 'Warsaw, Poland'."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: pattern
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the visual or design pattern of a creative work or product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A dress has a pattern of 'polka dot'. A fabric has a pattern of 'striped'. A flag has a pattern of 'Canadian flag'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork
candidates.comment: An encodes creative work relation between a media object and the creative work it represents or contains. Also called "represents work", "contains work", "media of work". Examples: "Video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "Audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Title'", "Image file encodesCreativeWork 'Painting Title'". Distinct from encoding, which is the inverse relation (CreativeWork -> MediaObject).

candidates.label: artworkSurface
candidates.comment: A supporting material or substrate for a visual artwork. Also called: art substrate, painting surface, canvas type. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Landscape' artworkSurface 'Canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artworkSurface 'Paper'", "VisualArtwork 'Mural' artworkSurface 'Wall'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: surface
candidates.comment: An identification of the material used as the surface for a visual artwork. Also called "artwork medium", "painting surface", "material base", "substrate". Examples: "The painting has surface canvas", "The drawing's surface is paper", "This artwork uses a wood surface."

candidates.label: mediaItemAppearance
candidates.comment: A media item appearance relation between a media review item and the specific media object(s) grouped within it. Also called: associated media, media objects, grouped items. Examples: "Fact Check Item mediaItemAppearance 'Image of politician'", "Video Analysis Item mediaItemAppearance 'Clip from broadcast'", "Audio Review Item mediaItemAppearance 'Sound recording'".

candidates.label: artMedium
candidates.comment: A material or technique used in the creation of a visual artwork. Also called: artistic medium, material used, technique. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Portrait' artMedium 'Oil on canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artMedium 'Pencil'", "VisualArtwork 'Digital Art' artMedium 'Digital'". Distinct from artform, which describes the general category of art.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: worksFor

candidates.label: foundingLocation

candidates.label: acquiredFrom

candidates.label: sourceOrganization

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog

Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". candidates.label: employee
